item.title: Global inflation debate puts BOJ rate-hike pace in spotlight
item.description: The Bank of Japan may face renewed pressure to increase the pace of interest rate hikes ahead of a key rate review this month, after global inflationary pressures from the Iran war and AI-driven demand shock dominated discussions at this week's IMF meetings.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan may face renewed pressure to increase the pace of interest rate hikes ahead of a key rate review this month, after global inflationary pressures from the Iran war and AI-driven demand shock dominated discussions at this week's IMF meetings. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda will bring home insights from his discussions with G7 and G20 colleagues in Bangkok, including what his US counterpart [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] described as a "common challenge" among global policymakers of dealing with inflation. "We have different tools, different sequences, but I would say if I look back over the last few months ... it was a synchronous tightening in monetary policy in most places around the world, and that means there's no free riders," Warsh said. Having just raised interest rates in September, many in the BOJ prefer to stand pat at its October 29-30 meeting to await more data on how past rate hikes have affected economic and financial conditions, [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"sources have told Reuters"]. Even so, the BOJ is likely to drop hawkish signals on the policy outlook that leave scope for a December hike, with the AI demand shock adding to inflationary pressures from high energy costs and rising import prices due to a weak yen, analysts say. Ueda will likely hold a news briefing later on Friday in Bangkok, which will be closely watched for clues on the pace and timing of future interest rate hikes. UPSIDE RISKS TO INFLATION During this week's annual meetings, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) highlighted the [USN:L1N45X05U TEXT:"resilience"] of the global economy against external shocks such as the Middle East war, with the pain mitigated by brisk AI-related demand. Global policymakers, however, also warned of the inflationary pressure from the AI boom that could warrant further monetary tightening - a message particularly relevant to the BOJ given its still-low borrowing costs. Such discussions may affect the BOJ's new quarterly growth and inflation projections due at this month's rate review, which may offer clues on how quickly it could raise rates ahead. Already, the BOJ has pivoted away from its cautious approach towards a policy more focused on combatting inflationary risks by hiking rates in June and September. And yet, at 1.25%, its policy rate means real borrowing costs are negative with inflation hovering around its 2% target and seen accelerating as firms pass on input costs to households. US Treasury Undersecretary [USN:P8N3W600D TEXT:"Erin Browne"] kept pressure on the BOJ to continue tightening to prevent disorderly yen falls, saying on Friday Japan must adjust its monetary policy to reflect that it no longer faces a deflationary environment. The US Federal Reserve's rate decision at its October 27-28 meeting could also affect the BOJ's debate through any impact on the yen, as the still-wide US-Japan rate divergence has caused the currency to weaken and increased import costs. BOJ board member [USN:L1N46101P TEXT:"Junko Koeda "]said on Thursday the central bank should not become overly cautious about raising interest rates given considerable upside risks to inflation, signalling the chance of a near-term hike in borrowing costs.

item.title: La nouvelle porte-parole de la Maison Blanche admet avoir échoué l'examen du barreau
item.description: La nouvelle porte-parole de la Maison blanche, Katie Zacharia, a déclaré jeudi soir qu'elle n'avait pas réussi l'examen du barreau, ce qui, selon la plupart des experts juridiques, lui interdit de prétendre au titre d'avocate alors qu'elle s'est initialement présentée comme telle.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La nouvelle porte-parole de la Maison blanche, Katie Zacharia, a déclaré jeudi soir qu'elle n'avait pas réussi l'examen du barreau, ce qui, selon la plupart des experts juridiques, lui interdit de prétendre au titre d'avocate alors qu'elle s'est initialement présentée comme telle. Katie Zacharia, qui a remplacé Karoline Leavitt et organisé mardi son premier point presse en tant que porte-parole de la Maison blanche, avait dit avoir exercé le métier d'avocate avant de se lancer dans la politique. Lors d'une interview sur la chaîne d'information Fox News, classée à droite et généralement favorable au président américain Donald Trump, elle a dit, en réponse à une question sur le sujet, avoir échoué l'examen du barreau. D'après l'université Pepperdine (Californie), où Katie Zacharia a fait ses études, elle a obtenu un diplôme de droit en 2011. Mais aux Etats-Unis, les diplômés en droit ne peuvent légalement exercer la profession d'avocat sans avoir été préalablement admis au barreau d'un Etat.

item.title: La Chine est prête à coopérer avec l'UE pour remédier aux déséquilibres mondiaux
item.description: La Chine est prête à engager un dialogue avec l'Union européenne (UE) pour améliorer la communication sur certains aspects de la gouvernance économique mondiale et de la coordination des politiques macroéconomiques, a déclaré vendredi le ministre chinois des Finances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Chine est prête à engager un dialogue avec l'Union européenne (UE) pour améliorer la communication sur certains aspects de la gouvernance économique mondiale et de la coordination des politiques macroéconomiques, a déclaré vendredi le ministre chinois des Finances. S'exprimant à Bangkok lors d'une réunion avec Valdis Dombrovskis, commissaire européen chargé de l’Economie et de la Productivité, Christine Lagarde, présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, et Kyriakos Pierrakakis, président de l’Eurogroupe, Lan Foan a déclaré que les déséquilibres mondiaux constituaient un "problème structurel économique complexe" de plus en plus influencé par des facteurs non économiques. "Toutes les parties devraient considérer ces déséquilibres de manière globale et objective", a ajouté le ministre chinois, appelant à une coopération ouverte et à une coordination des politiques macroéconomiques, précise un communiqué de son ministère. Cette réunion à Bangkok, en marge des assemblées annuelles du Fonds monétaire internationale et de la Banque mondiale, intervient une semaine après la conclusion d’un accord entre la Chine et l’Union européenne visant à limiter les exportations chinoises de voitures hybrides vers le bloc européen. L’UE cherche à réduire son déficit commercial avec la Chine, qui a atteint 360 milliards d’euros en 2025. Les dirigeants des pays membres de l'Union se réunissent vendredi à Bruxelles pour un deuxième jour de sommet européen abordant, entre autres, la question des relations commerciales avec Pékin.

item.title: UBS étudie des options à l'étranger au cas la réglementation suisse devient insupportable à ses yeux-sources
item.description: UBS étudie différents scénarios, dont un déménagement de son siège social ou une fusion avec une autre banque, au cas où la Suisse adopterait de nouvelles règles bancaires que le groupe jugerait excessivement strictes, selon trois sources proches du dossier.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: UBS étudie différents scénarios, dont un déménagement de son siège social ou une fusion avec une autre banque, au cas où la Suisse adopterait de nouvelles règles bancaires que le groupe jugerait excessivement strictes, selon trois sources proches du dossier. La Suisse élabore un projet de loi visant à instaurer des règles plus strictes afin d'éviter qu'un cas tel que la faillite de Credit Suisse ne se reproduise, en exigeant qu'UBS couvre l'intégralité de la valeur comptable de ses filiales étrangères en Suisse en fonds propres de première catégorie (CET1). Une commission de la chambre basse de l'Assemblée fédérale entamera, dans le courant du mois, l'examen des dispositions adoptées en septembre par la chambre haute, UBS ayant déjà laissé entendre qu'elle les jugeait intolérables. Un groupe au sein de la banque examine actuellement différentes options, parmi lesquelles figure l'établissement d'une liste de petites banques américaines qu'UBS pourrait éventuellement racheter, ainsi que la perspective d'un rachat de la banque elle-même, selon les sources. Aucune discussion n'est en cours à ce stade, ont précisé ces sources. UBS a déclaré ne pas commenter "les spéculations ni les opinions exprimées sur ces questions". Le quotidien Financial Times a rapporté vendredi que le gouvernement britannique avait discuté cette année avec UBS d'un possible déménagement à Londres si le groupe devait changer de siège social. UBS a obtenu en mars une licence bancaire américaine et souhaite développer ses activités dans le pays, mais les règles élaborées par Zurich visent notamment à réduire le risque auquel les contribuables suisses pourraient être exposés si la banque subissait des pertes aux États-Unis. La banque d'investissement américaine Morgan Stanley (MS.N) serait, en théorie, le partenaire idéal pour UBS, d'après des personnes proches de la réflexion. La banque suisse a déclaré à plusieurs reprises qu'elle n'envisageait pas de déménager et qu'elle accordait une grande importance à son ancrage en Suisse.

item.title: La UE se une en apoyo a Zelenski mientras Trump califica los ataques ucranianos de "vergüenza"
item.description: Los líderes de la Unión Europea se disponen a mostrar su apoyo al presidente Volodímir Zelenski en una cumbre que se celebrará el viernes, mientras el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, lanzaba otra andanada contra Ucrania, calificando de "vergüenza" sus ataques contra refinerías rusas.
item.dc:creator: Bart Meijer, Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: Los líderes de la Unión Europea se disponen a mostrar su apoyo al presidente Volodímir Zelenski en una cumbre que se celebrará el viernes, mientras el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, lanzaba otra andanada contra Ucrania, calificando de "vergüenza" sus ataques contra refinerías rusas. La UE recibe a Zelenski en Bruselas en uno de los momentos más difíciles para Ucrania, con una lluvia de misiles y drones sobre las ciudades ucranianas y el temor a que EEUU pueda retirar a Kiev el intercambio de información de inteligencia y el apoyo en materia de armamento. Trump tomó por sorpresa a Zelenski el pasado fin de semana al anunciar que Ucrania y Rusia habían acordado no atacar las instalaciones energéticas de la otra parte. De cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EEUU en noviembre, Trump ha culpado a los ataques ucranianos contra las refinerías rusas de provocar una subida de los precios de la energía que podría costarle votos en las urnas. "Queremos poner fin a esta guerra lo antes posible. Por el momento no vemos señales por parte de Rusia de que estén preparados para ello, para poner fin a esta guerra, por eso tenemos que prepararnos para el invierno", dijo Zelenski a su llegada a la cumbre. "El paquete de invierno no se limita a la energía, sino que también incluye la defensa aérea y la financiación", señaló Zelenski, y añadió que abordaría las necesidades de Ucrania para lo que queda de este año y para 2027. LA PREPARACIÓN PARA EL INVIERNO ESTARÁ EN LA AGENDA Ucrania atacó una refinería de petróleo rusa después de que Zelenski declarara que Kiev abandonaba el alto el fuego energético que Trump había anunciado, y criticara su disposición a llegar a acuerdos con Moscú. "Lo único que está haciendo es hacer que suba el precio mundial del petróleo. Bueno, creo que eso es una vergüenza", dijo Trump en una entrevista con el medio de comunicación Newsmax, después de que Ucrania atacara una refinería al sureste de Moscú que contribuye al abastecimiento de la capital rusa. El Gobierno de Trump también está considerando suavizar las sanciones a los denominados buques de la flota en la sombra que han transportado petróleo y productos petrolíferos desde países como Rusia, según dijo el miércoles un representante estadounidense. Los líderes de la UE han arremetido contra el acuerdo sobre el diésel de Trump, aunque ellos mismos se enfrentan a la escalada de los precios de la energía desde la guerra en Irán, lo que puso de manifiesto las divisiones entre los Estados miembros ya desde el primer día de la cumbre, el jueves. Zelenski dijo a Reuters a principios de este mes que Ucrania había acordado un plan con sus socios europeos que le permitiría cubrir un déficit de 27.000 millones de dólares en su gasto militar para este año, lo que le permitiría encargar los drones necesarios para continuar la lucha a principios de 2027. Sin embargo, el ministro de Finanzas, Sergii Marchenko, dijo recientemente que Ucrania aún se enfrentaba a un déficit presupuestario sin financiación para el próximo año de 32.600 millones de dólares, y eso sin incluir los 40.000 millones de dólares estimados en suministros militares directos de los aliados. "No estoy satisfecho con el número de países que se han mostrado dispuestos a comprometer nuevas ayudas financieras a Ucrania. Pero pronto veremos a varios países comprometerse a prestar más apoyo militar", dijo el primer ministro neerlandés, Rob Jetten. "Hoy nos centraremos más en hablar con Zelenski sobre cómo abordar la compleja situación diplomática que se ha planteado y cómo sobrevivir al invierno". Al ser preguntado por las últimas declaraciones de Trump, Jetten respondió: "Ese no es el lenguaje adecuado. Además, a Trump le conviene defender a Ucrania en esta guerra".

item.title: Kenya in talks for fresh multilateral financing, central bank chief says
item.description: Kenya is in discussions with several multilateral development banks to secure new financing that is expected to materialise in the current financial year, its central bank governor said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: Kenya is in discussions with several multilateral development banks to secure new financing that is expected to materialise in the current financial year, its central bank governor said on Friday. Governor Kamau Thugge said the government was in talks with the African Development Bank and the World Bank over potential budget support, including a World Bank Development Policy Operation (DPO). "They are looking at all kinds of financing... there's quite a number of sources that they are trying to access," Thugge said in an interview on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok. "Between now and June of next year is when that external financing will be expected." A debt-for-food swap is among the options being considered by the East African nation, Thugge said, without giving further details as he was not directly involved in the discussions. Reuters reported last month that Kenya is expected to receive about [USN:L8N44Y022 TEXT:"$400 million in emergency financing"] from the World Bank to help address risks including an Ebola outbreak in the region and El Niño-related disruptions. An IMF team is expected to visit Nairobi in December for a regular Article IV consultation mission, Thugge told Reuters, adding that a new programme with the Fund would be part of the discussions. "The IMF funding is not in any of our planning. But obviously, were it to come in, it would help in several ways," said Thugge. "It's cheaper than the alternative financing, especially domestic financing. It's concessional... and two, it also reduces the government's recourse to domestic borrowing, and maybe that can also help banks lend to the private sector a bit more." MONITORING INFLATION RISKS Thugge said there was still "enough time" to monitor developments in consumer price pressures, the ongoing Middle East war and weather conditions before deciding on its next rate move. The central bank last week maintained its [USN:L8N45T1AH TEXT:"benchmark lending rate"] (KECBIR=ECI) at 8.75% for the fourth policy meeting in a row, saying it saw inflation staying within its target range in the short term. But the country's energy regulator raised the maximum retail prices of petrol and diesel earlier this week, citing higher import costs linked to the Middle East conflict. Thugge said rising bond yields across developed markets could also contribute to inflationary pressures indirectly, by weighing on the domestic currency. "Definitely risks are tilted (to the upside)," said Thugge. "Even if there is an increase in the fuel (prices), the food prices have actually been trending downward, so one will still need to wait and see what happens to the food prices, and does the decline in food prices offset whatever increase there might be on fuel inflation." He expected Kenya's economy to grow 5% this year and 5.3% next year, compared with IMF forecasts of 4.5% and 4.7%, respectively, citing tailwinds in agriculture, industry and services. "It's likely our projection is closer to the truth than the IMF one."

item.title: Bayern are close to their best despite consecutive draws-coach Kompany
item.description: Bayern Munich are edging closer to their very best despite drawing their last two matches, coach Vincent Kompany said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayern Munich are edging closer to their very best despite drawing their last two matches, coach Vincent Kompany said on Friday. The German champions, who take on visitors RB Leipzig on Saturday, have drawn their last two matches in all competitions – a 2-2 against Augsburg that included conceding the [USN:L6N45W03O TEXT:"fastest goal"] in Bundesliga history, followed by a 3-3 at rank outsiders Viking in the Champions League on Tuesday. They looked far from convincing in both matches, missing chances and looking shaky at the back, and having to come from behind both times to rescue draws. They are currently in third spot in the Bundesliga, two points behind leaders Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund. "We want to attack," Kompany told a press conference. "We have the feeling that there are a lot of things behind the perception of these two results. I have the feeling it is just before we show our very best version. "In the last two matches we shot 50 times on goal. If we do a few things better then we are not too far from our very best version." Bayern have busy weeks coming up and after Leipzig – they face Arsenal in the Champions League before taking on leaders Freiburg in the Bundesliga. They then host Dortmund in Der Klassiker on October 31 after a German Cup second-round match against Magdeburg. "These moments that some people think might be difficult we say these are the best moments you can have in your career. If you win these matches then you have created some moments," Kompany said. "We are sharp and motivated... we look forward to these matches to measure ourselves against the best. "The lads reach the limit in every training session and it is fun to watch. They know it is now best to talk on the pitch."

item.title: MSCI unnecessarily throws Indonesia into a panic
item.description: The country's shares nosedived 11% after the index provider said it might kick the $570 bln stock market from its benchmark indices. Perhaps the Southeast Asian economy merits such a downgrade. But blindsiding the bourse and others on such a major decision should be verboten.
item.dc:creator: Hudson Lockett
item.content:encoded: Indonesia was already struggling to see through the toxic bushfire haze choking much of the country this week when it was blindsided by MSCI. In a terse announcement released on Friday in Asia, the index provider proposed ejecting the $570 billion equity market from its global benchmarks next year. Yet the move may end up chiefly throwing the spotlight on a lack of transparency and accountability among powerful index providers. That's counterproductive because MSCI’s frustration over Indonesia's lack of progress with its market reforms is entirely justified. Earlier this year the New York-based firm froze Indonesia’s weightings and [USN:S8N3UP04F TEXT:"threatened to downgrade"] it from Emerging to Frontier Market status due to opaque trading and ownership practices. So Friday's announcement that it had kicked off consultation over whether to reclassify Indonesia as a “standalone” market was an unnecessary shock. Not because MSCI's assessment is necessarily wrong. The company, run by Henry Fernandez for the past three decades, made clear the move came after feedback from market participants suggested even frontier status “would not properly recognize the depth of the market problems”. MSCI will go ahead with the expulsion unless its consultation over the next nine months “identifies clear evidence of material improvements in market governance and functioning to warrant reconsideration”. But it appears to have kept Indonesian institutions completely in the dark, a practice which ought to be verboten. It would be the first time, note analysts at Citi, that a country's stock market would be expelled primarily for perceived market integrity failures. This makes it all the more astounding that senior economic minister Airlangga Hartarto said MSCI [USN:L4N46124O TEXT:"had not mentioned"] any potential downgrade to standalone status during a meeting this week. Bourse head Jeffrey Hendrik also said he would seek further clarification on the basis for the announcement. The threat, which came a month ahead of a scheduled review, sent the Jakarta Composite Index (.JKSE) tumbling about 11%. That's the sharpest one-day fall since the 1998 Asian financial crisis and brought losses this year to about 40%. It could get worse: if Indonesia ends up joining the uninvestable likes of Argentina and Pakistan, passive investors tracking the MSCI Emerging Markets Index (.dMIEF00000PUS) , followed by funds worth some $1.4 trillion , would have to fully exit Indonesian stocks. Friday’s panicked selloff illustrates how badly flagged moves not only wrong-foot officials and exchanges whose cooperation is vital to reform; they can set off market shockwaves that reverberate far beyond the passive investors central to benchmark firms’ business. The move itself raises uncomfortable questions about how much power has been concentrated in the hands of index committee members at MSCI and peers like S&P Global and FTSE Russell. If Friday's move was meant to light a fire under Jakarta, perhaps it succeeded. Who exactly ends up getting unnecessarily burned as a result may be more of an open question than index firms expect. Follow Hudson Lockett on Bluesky and X . MSCI announced on October 16 that it had proposed reclassifying Indonesia to “standalone” market status, with a final decision to be reached by the end of June 2027 after a consultation period. The downgrade would fully remove the Asian stock market from the index provider’s global equity benchmarks. The announcement, which comes a month ahead of a scheduled review, escalates a previous warning that Indonesia could be moved from Emerging to Frontier Market status if it did not make sufficient progress addressing concerns over market dysfunction and enforcement. Funds worth about $1.4 trillion follow MSCI’s Emerging Markets Index, according to the company. The Jakarta Composite Index fell about 11% following the announcement, taking year-to-date losses for the country's equity market to more than 40%. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: China proposes adding 40 AI, biotech, solar technologies to export control list
item.description: China has proposed adding 40 technologies across the artificial intelligence, biomedicine and photovoltaic sectors to its catalogue of technologies prohibited or restricted from export, the commerce ministry announced on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China has proposed adding 40 technologies across the artificial intelligence, biomedicine and photovoltaic sectors to its catalogue of technologies prohibited or restricted from export, the commerce ministry announced on Friday. Public opinions are now being sought on the proposed revision until November 15 and China is simultaneously implementing interim pre-export registration management for the relevant technologies. Those included in the proposed revision are AI models, intelligent agents and computing clusters, which are the three fundamental building blocks of China's AI industry, at a time of increasing competition and geopolitical tensions with the United States over the technology's frontier development. In a separate statement, the ministry said the revision was proposed as applications of related technologies in sensitive fields are constantly expanding and that the move was routine and does not target any specific country, region or entity.

item.title: AFC eyes iron ore and uranium investments in Africa
item.description: The Africa Finance Corporation is looking for investments in iron ore and uranium as it seeks to expand its reach in critical minerals projects on the continent, the agency's head of mining and metals said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Africa Finance Corporation is looking for investments in iron ore and uranium as it seeks to expand its reach in critical minerals projects on the continent, the agency's head of mining and metals said. [USN:L5N3VX1DH TEXT:"Critical minerals"] have become a focal point of global competition, with the US and other major economies seeking to [USN:L6N42P0XG TEXT:"secure supply chains"] for electric vehicles and renewable energy while reducing dependence on China. Franklin Edochie, deputy director and head of mining at the Lagos-based continental financial institution, said the agency's interest in Africa's mining sector is broad, spanning precious and base metals as well as critical minerals. AFC already has interests in minerals such as gold, bauxite, copper and manganese across Africa, and now wants to add iron ore and uranium. Speaking on the sidelines of a mining conference in Cape Town, Edochie said combined output from Guinea, Liberia, Mauritania, and Sierra Leone could over the next 10 years "easily" equate to a top three iron ore producer in volume terms. "We are working towards financing those projects," he added. "Hopefully, within the next 6 to 12 months, we should be able to announce something (on uranium and iron ore investments).” AFC is also lead developer of the US-backed [USN:L8N41D299 TEXT:"Lobito minerals transport corridor"] linking African copper and cobalt mines to the Atlantic coast. The corridor will combine new and existing railway lines linking mines in Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo to Angola's Atlantic port of Lobito.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die Weltbank will sich stärker im Rohstoffbereich engagieren. Der Präsident der Entwicklungsbank, Ajay Banga, sagte am Freitag in Bangkok, das Geschäft mit kritischen Mineralen solle in den kommenden fünf Jahren verfünffacht werden. Es seien 20 Länder identifiziert worden, mit denen die Weltbank bei Projekten zur Erschließung kritischer Minerale zusammenarbeiten könne. "In dieser Woche haben wir unsere ersten Ländervereinbarungen mit Partner-Entwicklungsbanken geschlossen", sagte Banga. So sollten vor Ort Industrien unterstützt werden und Arbeitsplätze entstehen. Der neue Plan der Weltbank für Metalle und Minerale zielt auf eine Finanzierung von 19 Milliarden Dollar im Zeitraum von 2026 bis 2030 ab. Im Vergleichszeitraum von 2021 bis 2025 waren es 3,6 Milliarden Dollar gewesen. Die USA als größter Anteilseigner der Weltbank hatten diese zu einem stärkeren finanziellen Engagement in dem Bereich aufgefordert. US-Finanzminister Scott Bessent hatte zu Beginn der Woche erklärt, er wünsche sich eine größere Rolle der Weltbank bei der Förderung von Abbau- und Verarbeitungskapazitäten. Dies solle durch eine Risikominderung bei Projekten sowie durch Finanzierung und Investitionen in die notwendige Infrastruktur geschehen.

item.title: Altered image shared as Ilhan Omar mugshot after raid at her residence
item.description: An altered years-old image depicting Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar with a balding head was posted online as an authentic mugshot following a raid at her residence by Homeland Security Investigations on October 12.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: An altered years-old image depicting Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar with a balding head was posted online as an authentic mugshot following a raid at her residence by Homeland Security Investigations on October 12. US authorities conducted a [USN:L1N45Y0CB TEXT:"predawn raid"] at Omar’s Washington, DC, home as part of an ongoing Justice Department investigation, which a person familiar with the matter said was related to alleged immigration fraud. The altered image of Omar and an image depicting a head scarf in a police evidence bag were shared online after the raid, suggesting she was detained. Reuters previously [USN:KBN28S2S7 TEXT:"addressed"] the same altered image when it was shared in 2020. The altered version was created by combining an Associated Press photograph of Omar, where she is seen wearing the same earrings as in the altered image, and a mugshot of another man published in 2019 and credited to a police force in Wales. There are no credible reports of Omar being detained after the raid at her residence. A spokesperson in Omar’s Congressional office told Reuters in an email, “The Congresswoman was not detained.” A source close to the investigation also confirmed to Reuters that Omar was not detained. An analysis using OpenAI’s verification tool, which detects invisible watermarks embedded into the generated media, determined that both images were likely edited or created using the tech company’s AI models. The Department of Justice declined to comment. Verdict: Altered. An image purporting to show a mugshot of Ilhan Omar shared after a raid at her home in October 2026 is edited. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: G7-Länder planen Abwehrtests gegen KI-verstärkte Cyberangriffe auf Finanzbranche
item.description: Die sieben führenden Industrienationen (G7) planen Tests zur Abwehr von KI-unterstützten Cyberangriffen. Eine Vereinbarung dazu wurde am Rande der Herbsttagung des Internationalen Währungsfonds (IWF) in der thailändischen Hauptstadt Bangkok getroffen, sagte die japanische Finanzministerin Satsuki Katayama. Der IWF hatte diese Woche gewarnt, dass das Vertrauen in die Finanzbranche durch solche Cyberangriffe untergraben werden könnte.

item.content:encoded: Die sieben führenden Industrienationen (G7) planen Tests zur Abwehr von KI-unterstützten Cyberangriffen. Eine Vereinbarung dazu wurde am Rande der Herbsttagung des Internationalen Währungsfonds (IWF) in der thailändischen Hauptstadt Bangkok getroffen, sagte die japanische Finanzministerin Satsuki Katayama. Der IWF hatte diese Woche gewarnt, dass das Vertrauen in die Finanzbranche durch solche Cyberangriffe untergraben werden könnte. Die Pläne sehen Simulationen vor, die von den Finanzbehörden der G7-Staaten entwickelt werden. Erprobt werden sollen nach japanischen Angaben die Reaktionen auf Cyberangriffe, die mittels Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) verstärkt werden. Die Ergebnisse sollen die Wirksamkeit bestehender Vorgaben überprüfen und zur Überarbeitung genutzt werden. An den Übungen der Finanzministerien und Zentralbanken aus den G7-Staaten - das sind Deutschland, Frankreich, Italien, Großbritannien, die USA, Kanada und Japan - könnten auch private Geldhäuser beteiligt werden. Weltweit verstärken die Bankenaufsichtsbehörden derzeit ihre Bemühungen, KI-Risiken einzudämmen. Dazu gehört auch die Bank of England, die mit Geschäftsbanken auf der Insel an umfassenden Optionen zur Wiederherstellung nach Cyberangriffen arbeitet. Man könne nicht länger davon ausgehen, dass die eigene Abwehr immun gegen KI-gestützte Cyberangriffe sei, so die britische Zentralbank.

item.title: NHL roundup: Panthers' Brady Tkachuk caps 2nd straight hat trick in OT
item.description: Brady Tkachuk scored twice in the final nine minutes of regulation, then completed his second straight natural hat trick 2:23 into overtime, leading the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 come-from-behind victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday in Sunrise, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brady Tkachuk scored twice in the final nine minutes of regulation, then completed his second straight natural hat trick 2:23 into overtime, leading the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 come-from-behind victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday in Sunrise, Fla. Tkachuk is the first player since the Toronto Maple Leafs' Auston Matthews in February 2024 to record a hat trick in back-to-back games. He is the third Panther with a hat trick in consecutive games (Noel Acciari and Pavel Bure) and the second to complete a hat trick in overtime (Aleksander Barkov). Panthers goalie Akira Schmid, making his third consecutive appearance and second straight start while Jacob Markstrom remains day-to-day with an undisclosed injury, stopped 15 shots. Seth Jones logged two assists as the Panthers won two straight games for the first time this season. Liam Ohgren and Elias Pettersson scored for Vancouver, which took its sixth loss in a row (0-5-1). Canucks goalie Leevi Merilainen finished with 36 saves. Lightning 4, Kraken 3 (OT) Victor Hedman drove through the slot and scored at 2:07 of overtime as Tampa Bay beat Seattle and improved to 4-0-0 at home this season. Brandon Hagel potted two goals and Ilya Mikheyev notched his 100th career tally. Lightning goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy made 24 saves. All-time, the Lightning are 9-0-2 against the Kraken, while Vasilevskiy improved to 8-0-1 against them. Matty Beniers registered his 200th career point with a goal, and Ryan Winterton and Jared McCann also hit the net for the Kraken. Seattle goaltender Philipp Grubauer stopped 31 shots as the club slipped to 3-0-1 on its five-game road trip. Devils 7, Rangers 1 Luke Hughes led the way with two of New Jersey's four second-period goals to help bury New York in Newark, N.J. Nico Daws stopped 18 shots in the victory, while Nico Hischier, Arseny Gritsyuk, Evan Rodrigues, Cody Glass, and Stefan Noesen all joined Hughes on the scoresheet. Timo Meier, Dougie Hamilton, Brett Pesce, Dawson Mercer, and Amadeus Lombardi all picked up a pair of assists each. Pavel Dorofeyev scored the Rangers' lone goal as they allowed more than three goals for the first time this season. New York's starting goalie, Dylan Garand, permitted four goals on 13 shots. Senators 2, Islanders 1 (SO) Shane Pinto scored the only goal in the shootout for host Ottawa, which outlasted New York. Ridly Greig scored in the second period for the Senators. Linus Ullmark made 20 saves in regulation and overtime. Matias Maccelli scored for the second straight game for the Islanders. Semyon Varlamov, seeking his first win since Nov. 14, 2024, stopped 18 shots while falling to 0-1-1 on the season. Sabres 5, Maple Leafs 4 (OT) Owen Power scored in overtime as visiting Buffalo came from behind to top Toronto. Jack Quinn recorded four points, including two goals, and had a Gordie Howe hat trick for the Sabres after a second-period tussle with Troy Stecher. Mattias Samuelsson (a goal and an assist), Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson (two assists apiece) had multi-point games for Buffalo, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 26 saves. Kirill Marchenko produced a hat trick for Toronto, and Auston Matthews also scored. John Tavares had two assists but exited early in the third period after a collision with Josh Norris. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 29 shots. Blackhawks 4, Jets 3 (OT) Artyom Levshunov scored 97 seconds into overtime for Chicago, which beat Winnipeg to win its second straight game. Connor Bedard, in his second game of the season, scored a power-play goal and assisted on the game-winner. Frank Nazar and Ryan Donato also tallied for the Blackhawks, and Patrick Kane had two assists. Chicago goalie Spencer Knight made 31 saves. Neal Pionk finished with a goal and two assists for the Jets, who rallied from down two after a period to get a point. Kyle Connor and Alex Iafallo also scored, and Stuart Skinner stopped 24 shots. Wild 5, Blues 4 Matt Boldy scored his fifth career hat trick and added an assist as Minnesota held off St. Louis in Saint Paul, Minn. Kirill Kaprizov scored his third goal in two games and added two assists for the Wild, who have won three of four. Quinn Hughes and Joel Eriksson Ek each had two assists and Jesper Wallstedt made 21 saves. Kaprizov, who has six goals and five assists during a five-game point streak, headed to the dressing room late in the third period after being pushed into the boards. Robert Thomas had a goal and an assist and Mason McTavish scored his third goal in two games for the Blues, whose three-game point streak (2-0-1) ended. Cam Fowler had three assists, and Joel Hofer made 33 saves. Golden Knights 6, Flames 2 Mark Stone scored his second career regular-season hat trick and Jack Eichel had a short-handed goal and two assists as Vegas cruised past Calgary in Las Vegas. Ivan Barbashev tied his career high with three assists, Mitch Marner had two assists and Brett Howden and Braeden Bowman also scored goals for Vegas, which earned its sixth win in the past seven games. Carter Hart made 28 saves for the Golden Knights. Jake Middleton and Matt Coronato scored and Dustin Wolf finished with 27 saves for the Flames, who fell to 1-6-0 on the season. Sharks 3, Predators 2 (SO) Alex Nedeljkovic made 32 saves and kept Nashville from scoring in overtime and a shootout, helping visiting San Jose prevail. Mason Marchment and Will Smith scored in regulation before Macklin Celebrini registered the lone goal in the shootout for the Sharks, who had lost two in a row. Steven Stamkos scored with under a second left in regulation to tie the score for Nashville, sending the game to overtime. Ryan O'Reilly also scored and Juuse Saros made 30 saves for the Predators, who lost their third straight game (0-1-2). Red Wings 2, Flyers 1 Andrew Copp scored the go-ahead goal with 4:38 remaining in the third period, fueling host Detroit to a victory over winless Philadelphia. Anton Johansson scored his first career NHL goal and Daniil Tarasov made 17 saves for the Red Wings, who snapped a three-game winless streak (0-1-2). Matvei Michkov scored his team-leading third goal of the season and Joseph Woll turned aside 24 shots for the Flyers, who extended their franchise-record winless streak to start a season to nine games (0-6-3). They are one of two teams (the Los Angeles Kings) yet to win a game this season. Mammoth 4, Oilers 2 Clayton Keller scored twice and Logan Cooley netted his first goal of the season in a two-point performance, leading Utah to a victory at Edmonton. Barrett Hayton also scored for the Mammoth, who have won three consecutive games. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves, and Nick Schmaltz collected two assists. Leon Draisaitl and Shakir Mukhamadullin tallied for the Oilers, who had a five-game winning streak snapped. Devon Levi stopped 20 shots and saw the end of his franchise-record streak of four victories to start his time with Edmonton. --Field Level Media

item.title: IMF chief says AI risks may exceed opportunities without safeguards and ethical framework
item.description: The risks of artificial intelligence may exceed its opportunities if no adequate safeguards and ethical framework are put in place, IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said on Friday, backing a blend of industry self-regulation and input from key governments.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The risks of artificial intelligence may exceed its opportunities if no adequate safeguards and ethical framework are put in place, IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said on Friday, backing a blend of industry self-regulation and input from key governments. The nascent technology was a dominant topic at this week's annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, where the IMF on Tuesday flagged [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"significant growth and financial stability risks"] from a potential end of the AI investment boom, high debt levels and a prolonged war in the Middle East. During a panel discussion that included Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark, Georgieva said AI was already strengthening the global economy, but could also deliver [USN:L6N45Z0FI TEXT:"negative shocks"] if it failed to deliver major productivity gains as quickly as hoped. "If there are no safeguards, then the risks may exceed the opportunities. And above all, we do need an ethical foundation, and I'm not sure we are there as a society," she said. Certain preconditions needed to be put in place for people everywhere to benefit from the new and rapidly evolving technology, including [USN:L6N45N0Q6 TEXT:"access"] to digital infrastructure, access to electricity and adequate regulation, Georgieva said. The bigger question now was how to create guardrails for a technology that was evolving so rapidly, she said, likening AI developments to Formula One race cars careening around with no barriers to protect the audience. COMMON SENSE STANDARDS Industry self-regulation was appropriate, given that governments were not well-placed to regulate or oversee the constantly changing sector, but should include engagement with society. The countries with the biggest AI sectors, including the US, China and India, along with countries in the AI supply chain, should be involved, she told the panel. Institutions like the IMF should also be involved in their areas of competence, such as productivity growth, labour markets and financial stability risks, Georgieva said. "I think it's Formula One at night, without maybe brakes in the cars," quipped [USN:SPN46200F TEXT:"Anthropic's Clark"], picking up her analogy. He argued that setting standards was possible and was already starting through early policy frameworks in the European Union and voluntary commitments in the US. Clark said his company regularly tested its systems, published details on the tests and shared the information, but he did not believe it should be completely voluntary. Asked if he would favour regulation from the countries that produced AI, Clark said: "Yes. We need common sense standards, and that's how you ultimately give confidence in the technology and build the economy." He added that Anthropic had brought [USN:L6N461189 TEXT:"third-party evaluators"] into its business and given them permissions to review data. "That's ultimately what we think many others need to do," he said, welcoming a statement from Elon Musk that his firm SpaceX might do the same. ARTIFICIAL OR SUPER? US Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne said during a separate news conference that the IMF was too fixated on risks facing the global economy and should give more weight to opportunities for positive economic shocks, such as AI, which the US government is now calling "super intelligence." On Thursday, Browne told Reuters that Washington was in talks with other IMF shareholders about [USN:L1N4610GV TEXT:"adopting the new moniker"] in a joint statement being drafted by the fund's steering committee. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey told a meeting of the Institute of International Finance that he was more optimistic than a month ago that countries would reach alignment on testing standards for AI. "I'm not sure whether we're supposed to talk about AI now, are we? I did use the phrase the other day 'the artist formerly known as AI'," he said. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also weighed in, telling Georgieva during a separate panel: "Kristalina, you pronounce it AI. In the US we now pronounce it SI."

item.title: Italy prolongs Schengen suspension with Spain by another week
item.description: Italy has extended by a further week its suspension of the European Union's border-free arrangement with Spain, an Italian government source said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy has extended by a further week its suspension of the European Union's border-free arrangement with Spain, an Italian government source said on Friday. The extension aligns Italy with the countermeasure taken by Madrid, which has suspended its own Schengen arrangements with Rome until October 22. In the coming days the Italian and Spanish interior ministers will work to explore alternative forms of cooperation, the source added. Italy first suspended Schengen arrangements with Spain on July 31 and has repeatedly [USN:S8N3RN04D TEXT:"prolonged"] the measure, in response to a [USN:L1N43X0ZO TEXT:"mass surge"] in migrant arrivals into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco. Madrid criticised the move in August, describing Italy's actions as "[USN:L8N4440UI TEXT:"unjust"], contrary to European Union interests and discriminatory to the population of Spain".

item.title: El Banco Mundial quiere quintuplicar la financiación para minerales críticos para 2030, dice Banga
item.description: El presidente del Banco Mundial, Ajay Banga, dijo el viernes que la entidad de desarrollo se ha fijado la meta de quintuplicar su actividad en el sector de los minerales críticos en cinco años y ha identificado 20 países con los que puede colaborar en proyectos de desarrollo de esos recursos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente del Banco Mundial, Ajay Banga, dijo el viernes que la entidad de desarrollo se ha fijado la meta de quintuplicar su actividad en el sector de los minerales críticos en cinco años y ha identificado 20 países con los que puede colaborar en proyectos de desarrollo de esos recursos. Banga dio a conocer la nueva meta en un discurso preparado para una sesión plenaria de las reuniones anuales del Fondo Monetario Internacional y el Banco Mundial en Bangkok. "En minerales críticos, planeamos quintuplicar nuestra actividad en cinco años", dijo Banga. "Esta semana pusimos en marcha nuestros primeros acuerdos por país con bancos multilaterales de desarrollo asociados, para desarrollar industrias locales y lograr que más empleos y valor se queden en los países". El nuevo plan de ejecución del Banco Mundial para metales y minerales tiene como objetivo destinar 19.000 millones de dólares a la financiación de minerales críticos durante los ejercicios fiscales 2026-2030, frente a los 3.600 millones de los ejercicios 2021-2025. El desarrollo de minerales críticos es uno de los ámbitos a los que Estados Unidos, el mayor accionista del Banco Mundial, ha pedido que la entidad dedique más recursos financieros. El secretario del Tesoro estadounidense, Scott Bessent, dijo esta semana que quería que el banco desempeñara un papel más importante en el desarrollo de capacidad de extracción y procesamiento de minerales críticos mediante la reducción de los riesgos de los proyectos, su financiación y la inversión en la infraestructura necesaria. Señaló que esto incluye proyectos de minería en aguas profundas. Banga no mencionó la minería en aguas profundas, pero el plan del banco para los metales plantea un "enfoque de precaución" hacia este sector incipiente y añade que cualquier participación e inversión deben ajustarse a las políticas aplicables de la entidad. Banga repasó el aumento general de la financiación del Banco Mundial durante el ejercicio fiscal 2026, que terminó el 30 de junio, incluida la movilización de 112.000 millones de dólares de capital privado, más del triple que en el ejercicio fiscal 2022, antes de que asumiera el cargo. Sumada a los préstamos con cargo al propio balance del Banco Mundial, esa cifra elevó la financiación total del grupo a 230.000 millones de dólares en el ejercicio fiscal 2026, dijo.

item.title: Eutelsat shares extend rally after Ukraine's Starshield limits

item.content:encoded: Shares in European satellite operator Eutelsat (ETL.PA) soared again on Friday, having added a quarter in value this week after Ukraine [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"flagged speed limits"] on its military-grade Starlink satellite system, Starshield. item.title: Brésil Lula promet la gratuité des transports en commun le week-end
item.description: Le président brésilien Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a déclaré jeudi qu'il allait soumettre au Parlement un amendement constitutionnel garantissant la gratuité des transports publics le week-end, une nouvelle mesure à destination des revenus modestes avant le deuxième tour de l'élection présidentielle.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président brésilien Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a déclaré jeudi qu'il allait soumettre au Parlement un amendement constitutionnel garantissant la gratuité des transports publics le week-end, une nouvelle mesure à destination des revenus modestes avant le deuxième tour de l'élection présidentielle. Dans une vidéo publiée sur les réseaux sociaux, Lula, qui se présente pour un quatrième mandat, n'a toutefois pas précisé quand exactement il soumettrait cette proposition. Lors du premier tour de l'élection présidentielle, Flavio Bolsonaro, fils de l'ancien président d'extrême droite Jair Bolsonaro, a déjoué les pronostics en [USN:L8N45R001 TEXT:"devançant"] Lula. Un second tour aura lieu le 25 octobre. Les sondages donnent à ce stade Flavio Bolsonaro vainqueur mais si la deuxième enquête Datafolha publiée depuis la tenue du premier tour montre un resserrement de l'écart, avec 47% pour Flavio Bolsonaro et 45% pour Lula, contre un rapport de 49%-45% il y a une semaine. L'annonce d'une gratuité des transports en commun dans tout le pays le week-end intervient au lendemain de l'adoption à la quasi-unanimité par le Sénat d'un amendement constitutionnel visant à [USN:L6N4610I3 TEXT:"réduire"] la semaine de travail de six à cinq jours. Cette mesure, portée par Lula, a également été votée par Flavio Bolsonaro, qui siège actuellement au Sénat, alors qu'il avait longtemps exprimé son opposition à une réduction du temps de travail. Mardi, Lula a annoncé un projet de remise de dette pour les petits entrepreneurs. La semaine dernière, le gouvernement a prolongé d'un mois supplémentaire ses subventions sur les carburants et, le mois dernier, il a augmenté de 15% la "Bolsa Familia", un programme social destiné à lutter contre la pauvreté.

item.title: Bundestag beschließt Frühstartrente
item.description: Der Bundestag hat am Freitag mit der Mehrheit der Koalitionsfraktionen von CDU/CSU und SPD die sogenannte Frühstartrente beschlossen. Januar 2027 in Kraft treten.
