item.title: China's Tencent says AI agents showed unintended browsing behaviour
item.description: Tencent said on Friday that AI agents used to evaluate third-party models displayed web-browsing behavior not intended by the tech giant, in what appears to be the first known incident of rogue agent actions acknowledged by a major Chinese company.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Tencent (0700.HK) said on Friday that AI agents used to evaluate third-party models displayed web-browsing behavior not intended by the tech giant, in what appears to be the first known incident of rogue agent actions acknowledged by a major Chinese company. The statement followed a report by AI-safety research group Swarmchasers on Wednesday, which said "rogue" agents running on infrastructure it linked to Tencent Cloud made repeated attempts between September 28 and October 8 to retrieve information from Alibaba's (9988.HK) Amap, China's equivalent to Google Maps. Tencent Hunyuan, the company's artificial intelligence unit, said in a post on X that the activity did not originate from its Hunyuan models. Its review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination, it said. The Swarmchasers researchers said the agents sought information such as the commonly used entrances at Chinese parks, museums and zoos. The actions are not as egregious as those disclosed by US AI companies which include the [USN:L1N44N0YE TEXT:"hack"] of open-source platform Hugging Face by an OpenAI agent and the lodging of a [USN:L6N45V11M TEXT:"fake homicide tip"] by an Anthropic agent. But the disclosure underscores [USN:L6N45E0SV TEXT:"research"] that shows Chinese AI agents can also misrepresent their identity, conceal failures and try to circumvent testing controls. Tencent said it took the findings very seriously and was strengthening network access controls and agent monitoring. Hunyuan is one of China's leading AI model developers, competing with in-house teams at rivals such as Alibaba and ByteDance. ByteDance this week announced [USN:L8N4610P8 TEXT:"the creation"] of a new unit focused on AI model and agent safety. Swarmchasers said it used the word "rogue" to describe agents taking actions outside their intended scope or completing a task in unintended ways. After routine automated requests were blocked, the agents tried other methods, including public web tools that could open pages and run code, routing requests through other websites and using Amap keys and security codes found in publicly available software code. Swarmchasers said it found no evidence that the agents breached Amap's main anti-bot safeguards. Most of the 2,818 attempts it recorded either failed or returned anti-bot pages, login screens or blank results. Some requests returned information through cached pages and intermediary services, including data on visitor arrivals at Chengdu Zoo, Swarmchasers said. The researchers said they could not determine whether an agent read the result or completed its task. Alibaba declined to comment.

item.title: Rogue AI agents broke into Indian firms' live systems, government says
item.description: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide. AI model providers had voluntarily disclosed that their agents "exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks" during test runs to access Indian firms' data, including business records, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said late on Thursday. It did not name the providers or the affected organisations. The disclosure brings India into a growing global debate over how AI companies test models with advanced hacking abilities. OpenAI said in July its models [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"went rogue"] during testing and breached a startup, while Anthropic has disclosed at least four [USN:L4N4511Q1 TEXT:"instances"] of AI models' hacking external systems so far this year. OpenAI has also [USN:L4N45L03J TEXT:"apologised"] for the hacking of an Australian government website by its rogue AI agent. None of the affected Indian entities detected the intrusions themselves, and in every case it was the AI companies that flagged the incidents, CERT-In said. In a second set of cases, the government agency's own investigations found attackers deliberately using freely available AI tools to probe Indian systems and break in for financial gain, with such tools deployed widely across infrastructure in multiple countries. Attacks that once took days from first entry to final damage were compressed to a few hours, CERT-In said, and victims that failed to fully clean up were attacked again within days, at greater depth.

item.title: Turtles offer early warning from a warming Mediterranean ahead of COP31
item.description: Under a moonlit sky, turtle hatchlings emerge from the sand on Turkey's Mediterranean coast and scramble towards the sea, taking part in an ancient natural cycle that scientists say is increasingly being shaped by climate change.
item.dc:creator: Daren Butler, Bulent Usta
item.content:encoded: Under a moonlit sky, turtle hatchlings emerge from the sand on Turkey's Mediterranean coast and scramble towards the sea, taking part in an ancient natural cycle that scientists say is increasingly being shaped by climate change. Throughout the night, sea turtle biologist Yakup Kaska and his team of volunteers monitor activity in the nests. Pyramid-shaped cages protect the eggs buried in the sand from foxes that roam the 4-km (2.5-mile) Iztuzu sandbar, a tourist beach by day and haven for turtle conservation by night. The loggerhead turtle, which nests on shores across the Mediterranean, is the mascot of COP31, the annual UN climate summit that Turkey hosts next month. Marine conservation will be a key focus of the gathering along the coast in Antalya. Researchers say the turtle illustrates how climate change is altering ecosystems in the Mediterranean, which has experienced a long-term warming trend since the early 1980s. THE SEA TURTLE AS CLIMATE BAROMETER A Reuters analysis showed European waters had their [USN:L6N4510XR TEXT:"hottest summer months on record"] with severe consequences for some coastal communities. Researchers say climate change is also steadily warming nesting beaches across the Mediterranean. The sex of turtle hatchlings is determined by nest temperature. Warming sands produce more females. "Sea turtles provide us with a very rapid warning system," said Uskudar University ecology lecturer Ayfer Sirin, who has carried out extensive research on loggerheads. She said they reflect environmental changes affecting coastal and marine ecosystems because they depend on both land and sea. In a five-year doctoral study at Pamukkale University, Sirin found that warming temperatures were linked to earlier nesting, shorter incubation periods and a predominance of females. The study at Patara beach estimated that on average some 70% of loggerhead hatchlings were female and concluded that behavioural adjustments alone may not be enough to offset the effects of climate change. Nest temperatures at Iztuzu rose by nearly 1 degree Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit) over the past 20 years, Kaska said, adding that broader analysis suggested females accounted for as many as 80-90% of hatchlings in many sea turtle populations. Scientists say there is a risk that continued warming may eventually produce too few males to support successful reproduction. Another hazard is that nest temperatures above 30 C (86 F) increase the risk of embryo mortality, Sirin said. According to the Marine Turtle Specialist Group, loggerheads are classified as vulnerable globally. Those in the Mediterranean are listed among those of least concern, reflecting conservation gains, but scientists say climate change is creating new pressures. CROSS-BORDER HABITATS AND COOPERATION The turtles' migratory lifestyle illustrates the need for cross-border cooperation at COP31, Kaska said. "They might be nesting in Turkey, but they are feeding in Tunisia or they are feeding in the Adriatic and so on," he said, calling on countries to collaborate to protect Mediterranean biodiversity. COP31 President Murat Kurum, Turkey's environment minister, told an Ocean and Seas conference last month: "Protecting the oceans is a responsibility we all share. We call on every party to turn that responsibility into bold, concrete action: restoring ecosystems and building resilience." Turkey has set a goal of reaching net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2053 and has highlighted the expansion of renewable energy as a key element of its climate strategy. HAZARDS FROM FISHING NETS TO PLASTIC Female loggerhead turtles typically return decades later to nest on the beaches where they hatched, but ecosystem changes mean some are nesting farther north, where they were previously uncommon, Kaska said. However, Iztuzu remains a key location with about 30,000 hatchlings entering the sea each season from hundreds of nests. On the beach, volunteers monitor the hatchlings, using dim red lights to minimise disturbance as they navigate towards the waves. In the sea, the hatchlings face further threats, including from fishing nets, boats and plastic waste. "A sea turtle caught in a fishing net cannot come up for air and unfortunately dies by drowning," Sirin said. A short walk from Iztuzu beach, injured turtles recover in large circular pools at the Dekamer rehabilitation centre, where veterinarians treat injuries, including from boat propellers. Plastic pollution is a particular concern. Kaska said 60% of turtles brought to the centre have at least five pieces of plastic in their digestive systems. "Throwing a plastic bag in the sea is like throwing a bullet for the turtles," he said. For researchers, the turtles are a visible measure of the health of the Mediterranean ecosystem. As dawn approaches, a final group of hatchlings disappears into the waves. If they survive, some may return decades from now to nest.

item.title: Money transfer firm Wise raises revenue growth outlook as cross-border volumes jump
item.description: Money transfer firm Wise , said on Thursday it expects full-year revenue growth to come in at the upper end of its target range after strong customer growth and higher cross-border transaction volumes boosted second-quarter revenue.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Money transfer firm Wise (WISEa.L) , said on Thursday it expects full-year revenue growth to come in at the upper end of its target range after strong customer growth and higher cross-border transaction volumes boosted second-quarter revenue. Wise now expects fiscal 2027 net revenue growth near the upper end of its 15% to 20% target range and maintained its income-before-tax margin outlook near the top of its 20% to 25% range The update reflects rising demand for low-cost international payments as consumers and businesses move more money across borders and hold more funds on digital platforms Cross-border payment volumes rose 22% to $71.7 billion, while active customers increased 20% to 12.5 million However, the cross-border take rate, a measure of revenue earned from each dollar transferred, fell to 0.49% from 0.52% a year earlier as the company cut prices to attract new customers Wise has been expanding its global payments network, but its US growth ambitions suffered a setback in July after regulators [USN:L6N43Q0F7 TEXT:"denied"] its application to create a national trust bank. The company said it intends to reapply for the licence Net revenue grew 21% to $739.1 million during the second quarter, while customer holdings rose 28% to $43.5 billion

item.title: UK watchdog moves to protect energy market from wholesale price swings
item.description: The British energy regulator Ofgem on Friday launched a consultation on activating its market stabilisation charge, to protect energy suppliers from wholesale price swings and continued market volatility during a possibly tough winter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The British energy regulator Ofgem on Friday launched a consultation on activating its market stabilisation charge, to protect energy suppliers from wholesale price swings and continued market volatility during a possibly tough winter. Here are some details from the regulator's statement: The mechanism protects suppliers from losses when energy prices fall sharply by compensating suppliers that bought energy in advance if customers switch to cheaper deals Ofgem reintroduced the mechanism in May, after wholesale energy prices soared due to the Iran conflict The consultation seeks views on the proposed activation and how it should operate, including trigger levels, notice periods and deactivation arrangements Ofgem said activating the mechanism would not automatically increase customer bills, with payments between suppliers only occurring if wholesale prices were to fall substantially "We're preparing for what is likely to be a difficult winter for many households," said Neil Kenward, interim director general of markets at Ofgem The mechanism previously operated between April 2022 and March 2024 to protect markets from price volatility triggered by the Russia-Ukraine war

item.title: La orden de limitar Starshield en Ucrania procedió de la Casa Blanca, según fuentes
item.description: La orden de limitar un sistema de satélites utilizado por Ucrania para las comunicaciones en el campo de batalla y las operaciones con drones procedió de la propia Casa Blanca, según dos funcionarios estadounidenses y un funcionario occidental informados sobre el asunto.
item.dc:creator: Erin Banco, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: La orden de limitar un sistema de satélites utilizado por Ucrania para las comunicaciones en el campo de batalla y las operaciones con drones procedió de la propia Casa Blanca, según dos funcionarios estadounidenses y un funcionario occidental informados sobre el asunto. Las fuentes dijeron que los responsables del Departamento de Defensa recibieron un mensaje en el que se indicaba que era necesario ralentizar el servicio Starshield de SpaceX destinado al ejército ucraniano. Los funcionarios, que hablaron bajo condición de anonimato, no especificaron quién en la Casa Blanca tomó la decisión ni quién fue el responsable de ejecutar la orden. El Pentágono es el mayor cliente de Starshield, que es la versión de grado militar del servicio Starlink. Funcionarios ucranianos afirmaron esta semana que los receptores Starlink de grado militar dejaron de funcionar en Ucrania cuando se montaron en objetos que se desplazaban a gran velocidad, lo que interfería en el rendimiento de los drones ucranianos que dependen de ellos para sus sistemas de guía a bordo sobre el territorio ucraniano. Una persona del Ministerio de Defensa de Ucrania dijo el jueves que los receptores ya funcionaban en movimiento, pero solo a velocidades de hasta 160 kilómetros por hora. EEUU PRESIONA A UCRANIA POR LOS ATAQUES A REFINERÍAS La decisión de restringir temporalmente este sistema de comunicaciones vital se produjo después de que el presidente Donald Trump presionara a Kiev para que detuviera sus ataques contra las refinerías rusas, a las que ha culpado del aumento vertiginoso de los precios de la energía, que está mermando las perspectivas de su Partido Republicano de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre. Sin embargo, los expertos afirman que el repunte de los costos energéticos se debe principalmente a la guerra de EEUU e Israel contra Irán, que ha provocado ataques iraníes contra instalaciones energéticas y ha cerrado en gran medida el vital estrecho de Ormuz. En respuesta a una solicitud de comentarios sobre la orden de limitar Starshield, un alto cargo estadounidense dijo: "El presidente nunca hizo tal petición". La Casa Blanca no respondió a las preguntas sobre si otros funcionarios del Gobierno podrían haber formulado dicha solicitud. Starshield fue desarrollado por SpaceX específicamente para clientes del Gobierno y de la seguridad nacional, en particular el Departamento de Defensa de EEUU. Starshield utiliza la constelación Starlink como columna vertebral de su sistema. Autoridades ucranianas afirmaron que las restricciones complicaban las misiones de ataque contra las fuerzas y la logística rusas en el territorio ocupado y ralentizaban los drones interceptores utilizados para derribar los drones rusos Shahed que se acercaban. Elon Musk, director ejecutivo de SpaceX, dijo el miércoles en la red social X que, dado que los sistemas Starshield son propiedad de Estados Unidos y están bajo su control, cualquier limitación en cuanto a velocidad o uso la decide el ejército estadounidense o el presidente. SpaceX no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. El Departamento de Defensa y la embajada de Ucrania en Washington tampoco respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios. DETERIORO DE LAS RELACIONES Las relaciones entre Kiev y Washington se han deteriorado en los últimos días tras una reunión celebrada en Miami el 9 de octubre, a la que acudieron representantes de ambos países, así como de Europa y del Banco Mundial. Jared Kushner, yerno de Trump, y Steve Witkoff, enviado del Gobierno de Trump para Oriente Medio, adoptaron un tono duro con Ucrania en la reunión, según otra persona familiarizada con el asunto. Comunicaron a los funcionarios ucranianos que Estados Unidos estaba frustrado por los continuos ataques de Kiev contra refinerías rusas, a pesar de las reiteradas peticiones de Washington para que cesaran. La delegación estadounidense también explicó la decisión de Washington de cerrar un acuerdo sobre diésel con Rusia, afirmando que la Casa Blanca esperaba que esto suavizara la postura de Moscú respecto a las negociaciones de paz. Ese acuerdo, en virtud del cual Rusia suministrará más de 2,25 millones de barriles de diésel a los mercados estadounidenses y mundiales, ha desencadenado una reacción negativa por parte de algunos parlamentarios estadounidenses, que afirman que proporcionará a Moscú fondos para continuar con su guerra sin obligar al presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, a hacer concesiones para poner fin al conflicto. En los días siguientes, el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, y Trump se criticaron mutuamente; Zelenski calificó de "débil" la decisión de EEUU sobre el acuerdo del diésel ruso. Trump pidió que se celebraran elecciones en Ucrania y la destitución de Zelenski. Entre bastidores, funcionarios estadounidenses amenazaron con dejar de proporcionar a Kiev información de inteligencia sobre los lanzamientos de misiles rusos, que Ucrania utiliza para frustrar los ataques, tal y como informó anteriormente Reuters. Trump dijo el martes que Washington seguía compartiendo información de inteligencia con Ucrania. Tras la medida para restringir el acceso de Ucrania a Starshield, los ucranianos realizaron llamadas el martes y el miércoles para obtener respuestas de altos funcionarios de la Casa Blanca, el Departamento de Estado y el Pentágono, según un alto cargo ucraniano, quien añadió que a Kiev se le comunicó que se trataba de una decisión de la Casa Blanca. El Pentágono ha gastado miles de millones de dólares en los servicios Starlink y Starshield. También ha adquirido satélites Starshield específicos, entre ellos naves espaciales de comunicaciones para misiones de alerta de misiles y una constelación de espionaje para la Oficina Nacional de Reconocimiento, según informó Reuters en 2024.

item.title: South African president reinstates suspended police chief
item.description: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Friday he was reinstating the country's police chief, six months after he was suspended over charges he broke public finance rules in the irregular awarding of a tender.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Friday he was reinstating the country's police chief, six months after [USN:L1N4160XY TEXT:"he was suspended"] over charges he broke public finance rules in the irregular awarding of a tender. Fannie Masemola, national commissioner of the South African Police Service since 2022, will resume his duties on Monday after prosecutors withdrew charges linked to a 228 million-rand ($13.85 million) police health services contract. The presidency said prosecutors ordered the withdrawal of charges against Masemola last month, with a local court in Pretoria formally withdrawing the case shortly thereafter. Prosecutors had accused Masemola of failing to comply with financial oversight and procurement controls linked to a police health services contract awarded to Medicare24, allegations he denied. The contract became a focal point of the Madlanga Commission, which is investigating allegations that criminal syndicates infiltrated parts of South Africa's law-enforcement and criminal justice system. item.title: Mehr Genehmigungen für Wohnungsbau - "Erholen uns von historischem Tief"

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lichtblick für den deutschen Wohnungsbau: Der seit über einem Jahr anhaltende Aufwärtstrend bei den Genehmigungen hat sich im August fortgesetzt. Die Zahl stieg um 6,8 Prozent im Vergleich zum Vorjahresmonat auf 20.600, wie das Statistische Bundesamt am Freitag mitteilte. Das ist bereits der 15. Anstieg in Folge. Von Januar bis August gaben die Behörden damit grünes Licht für den Bau von 169.400 Wohnungen in neuen sowie bereits bestehenden Gebäuden, ein Plus von 12,1 Prozent zum Vorjahreszeitraum. "Das klingt nach viel, ist aber noch immer rund ein Drittel weniger als 2021, als im selben Zeitraum über 250.000 Wohnungen genehmigt wurden", sagte der Hauptgeschäftsführer des Zentralverbands des Deutschen Baugewerbes (ZDB), Felix Pakleppa. Höhere Zinsen und Materialkosten hatten in den vergangenen Jahren viele Bauherren abgeschreckt. "Wir erholen uns von einem historischen Tiefpunkt, von einem normalen Niveau sind wir noch weit entfernt", sagte Pakleppa. Auch in diesem Jahr sind die Bauzinsen gestiegen, nachdem die Europäische Zentralbank (EZB) ihren Leitzins wegen der erhöhten Inflationsgefahren zweimal angehoben hat - im Juni und zuletzt im September auf aktuell 2,50 Prozent. Viele Experten halten es deshalb für fraglich, ob die Genehmigungen auch tatsächlich alle umgesetzt werden. "Eine genehmigte Wohnung ist nicht automatisch eine gebaute Wohnung", sagte Pakleppa. Ende 2025 hätten rund 450.000 genehmigte Wohnungen auf Eis gelegen, weil sich der Bau für viele nicht rechne. "HÖHERE FINANZIERUNGSKOSTEN BELASTEN" Die Stimmung im deutschen Wohnungsbau hat sich im September angesichts steigender Zinsen eingetrübt. Das Barometer für das Geschäftsklima fiel auf minus 25,1 Punkte von minus 22,5 Zählern im August, wie das Münchner Ifo-Institut zu seiner Umfrage mitteilte. Besonders die Geschäftsaussichten für die kommenden Monate wurden von den Unternehmen skeptischer gesehen, ihre aktuelle Lage bewerteten sie weitgehend gleich. "Die Zinserhöhung der EZB dürfte die Zuversicht im Wohnungsbau gedämpft haben", sagte Ifo-Umfragechef Klaus Wohlrabe. "Die Aussicht auf wieder höhere Finanzierungskosten belastet die Branche." In den Auftragsbüchern ist eine Belebung noch nicht zu erkennen. Der Anteil der Unternehmen, die über einen Auftragsmangel klagen, blieb im September unverändert bei 41,3 Prozent. Gleichzeitig wurden wieder etwas mehr Projekte storniert, fand das Ifo-Institut heraus: 14,1 Prozent der Unternehmen berichteten von abgesagten Aufträgen, nach 13,4 Prozent im August. Den größten prozentualen Zuwachs gab es in den ersten acht Monaten bei den Zweifamilienhäusern, wo die Zahl der genehmigten Wohnungen um 21,7 Prozent auf 10.000 stieg. Auch bei den Einfamilienhäusern war ein merklicher Anstieg um 7,8 Prozent auf 31.500 Genehmigungen zu verzeichnen. In Mehrfamilienhäusern, die den größten Anteil am Neubau ausmachen, zogen die behördlichen Zusagen um 14,5 Prozent auf 90.600 Wohnungen an. Hoffnungen setzt die Baubranche auf den sogenannten Gebäudetyp E - das E steht dabei für einfach oder experimentell. Hier soll auf überflüssige Standards verzichtet werden, um schneller und billiger bauen zu können. Der Zentrale Immobilien Ausschuss (ZIA) fordert eine rechtssichere Ausgestaltung. "Wir brauchen Tempo und können es uns nicht länger leisten, das Potenzial, das im Gebäudetyp E liegt, in der Warteschleife verkümmern zu lassen", sagte ZIA-Hauptgeschäftsführerin, Aygül Özkan.

item.title: India's derivatives trading volumes may recover after settlement rule changes, analysts say
item.description: The Indian markets regulator's decision to revert to the volume-weighted average price method to determine settlement prices of derivatives contracts on expiry days could reduce volatility and help revive volumes, according to analysts.
item.dc:creator: Vivek M
item.content:encoded: The Indian markets regulator's decision to revert to the volume-weighted average price method to determine settlement prices of derivatives contracts on expiry days could reduce volatility and help revive volumes, according to analysts. The Securities and Exchange Board of India said that from December 7, derivatives contracts on expiry days will once again be settled using the volume-weighted average price of the last 30 minutes of regular trading. The move follows backlash from traders amid sharp swings in stock and index levels after the closing auction session (CAS) was implemented on August 3, which prompted some to scale back on trading activity. Total derivatives turnover on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSEI.BO) fell 19.2% month-on-month to 34.48 trillion rupees ($363.37 billion) in August, following the introduction of CAS. This added to a [USN:L4N43G0S4 TEXT:"decline"] in volumes due to tighter regulations on lending to proprietary traders and higher transaction taxes. "This (changes to CAS) should reduce expiry-day volatility under the closing auction session, benefiting brokers whose orders remain below pre-CAS levels," brokerage firm Jefferies said. Analysts now expect volumes to return to pre-CAS levels, although the extent of the recovery remains uncertain. "The options traders who had moved away from the system may start coming back," said Raj Deepak Singh, vice president of derivatives and quantitative research at ICICI Direct. Under the revised rules, trading in index derivatives will continue until 3:45 p.m. IST, except on expiry days when trading will end at 3.30 p.m. IST, SEBI said. Shares of exchange operators BSE (BSEL.NS) and National Stock Exchange of India fell 1.7% and 0.6%, respectively, on Friday, while those of brokerage firms were mixed. Angel One (ANGO.NS) fell 2.7% and Groww (BILO.NS) rose 1.2%. ($1 = 94.8900 Indian rupees)

item.title: Man Group's assets under management hit record $270.9 billion, volatility drives inflows
item.description: Hedge fund Man Group shares rose 3% on Friday after reporting its assets under management hit a record $270.9 billion at the end of September, beating expectations and marking a rise of 6.8% from three months earlier, as volatile markets drove inflows.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hedge fund Man Group (EMG.L) shares rose 3% on Friday after reporting its assets under management hit a record $270.9 billion at the end of September, beating expectations and marking a rise of 6.8% from three months earlier, as volatile markets drove inflows. AUM at London-listed Man Group, which makes money from management fees, rose 26% year on year, and were above the company compiled consensus of $263 billion, according to Citi. Investors added $10.1 billion to Man Group's funds in the quarter, above expectations, $1.9 billion to its alternative funds, and $8.2 billion to its long only funds. $5.9 billion of the AUM increase was made up of investment performance. "We see Man as a key beneficiary of a more volatile market environment and growing investor demand for liquid (alternatives)," said Citi, who described the results as strong. The third quarter was volatile for global markets, as oil pushed back above $100 a barrel on Iran war jitters. September saw a dramatic government bond selloff, as investors processed a growing [USN:L8N45U1VY TEXT:"government debt"] burden, inflation fanned by high energy costs and competition for capital from a global data-centre boom. Investor attitudes towards the tech sector also waxed and waned in the quarter as they tried to assess the implications of companies' huge spending on AI for both buyers of chips and those that sell them.

item.title: Warsh, de la Fed, ve fortaleza económica en EEUU, pero no adelanta decisión sobre tasas
item.description: El presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, se mostró optimista el viernes respecto a la solidez de la economía estadounidense y se sorprendió de lo bien que las economías mundiales han "aguantado" en medio de las recientes crisis geopolíticas, a pesar de la política monetaria más restrictiva adoptada para combatir la inflación.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, se mostró optimista el viernes respecto a la solidez de la economía estadounidense y se sorprendió de lo bien que las economías mundiales han "aguantado" en medio de las recientes crisis geopolíticas, a pesar de la política monetaria más restrictiva adoptada para combatir la inflación. "He salido de las reuniones celebradas aquí ayer y hoy, y es difícil mantener una conversación con responsables de bancos centrales sin comparar impresiones y escuchar lo mismo sobre el repunte de los precios", dijo Warsh. Dado que la inflación es un "reto común", señaló en las reuniones anuales de 2026 del FMI y el Banco Mundial celebradas en Bangkok, los bancos centrales de todo el mundo llevaron a cabo "un endurecimiento sincronizado de la política monetaria en la mayoría de los lugares del mundo, lo que significa que no hay quien se salga con la suya". En Estados Unidos, señaló, "dejamos muy claro que garantizaríamos la estabilidad de precios y, hace aproximadamente un mes, retiramos una parte de la política expansionista", en referencia a la subida de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal en septiembre. SIN INDICIOS DE QUE SE NECESITEN MÁS SUBIDAS DE TASAS Sin embargo, fiel a su estilo desde que asumió el cargo de presidente de la Fed en mayo, no dio ninguna pista sobre si cree que serán necesarias más subidas de tasas de interés, ni sobre cuándo. "No me adelanto a las reuniones", añadió Warsh. "No creo en decir ahora lo que podría hacer en las reuniones que tengamos durante el resto del año". Los colegas de Warsh en la Fed no se han mostrado reticentes a la hora de expresar sus opiniones sobre la trayectoria de las tasas. En las últimas semanas, casi todos han afirmado que probablemente sea necesario un mayor endurecimiento, pero la mayoría quería disponer de más datos económicos para evaluar la tendencia de la inflación, lo que indica que era poco probable que aplicaran una segunda subida de tasas este mes. Los mercados financieros han tenido en cuenta esas declaraciones y apuestan por que la Fed esperará hasta diciembre para subir las tasas. Esto siguió siendo así incluso después de que los informes de esta semana mostraran que dos indicadores diferentes de la inflación se situaban por encima de lo esperado y se alejaban del objetivo del 2% de la Fed. TEMAS ECONÓMICOS MÁS AMPLIOS La decisión de Warsh de eludir por completo la próxima decisión de política monetaria y ceñirse a temas económicos más amplios mantiene intacta la expectativa de que la Fed no subirá las tasas de interés este mes. Abordó aspectos como el impacto de la inteligencia artificial, la necesidad de mantener la estabilidad financiera y las perspectivas sobre el crecimiento de Estados Unidos y la capacidad de resistencia de la economía mundial. "Creo que en Estados Unidos la economía real, gracias a esa resiliencia que has mencionado, pero también a un auge de la inversión —que no se limita solo a la inteligencia artificial—, ese auge de la inversión se está extendiendo", dijo Warsh en una conversación con Kristalina Georgieva, directora gerente del Fondo Monetario Internacional. "Eso significa que contamos con numerosos factores favorables que aportan cierta fortaleza y durabilidad a esta economía. (...) Ese tipo de impulso ciertamente no se encuentra en todas partes del mundo". Warsh dijo que la economía mundial estaba "mostrando una capacidad de resistencia que no estoy seguro de haber previsto hace cinco o seis meses, dado lo que está ocurriendo en el ámbito geopolítico y en los focos de tensión de todo el mundo". "Estamos viendo elementos comunes y estamos tomando medidas, y considero que eso es algo positivo", añadió. "Creo, con optimismo —quizá les parezca ingenuo—, que, al menos en Estados Unidos, vamos a salir de esto fortalecidos, con una economía más sólida a largo plazo y más capaz de liderar el crecimiento económico mundial".

item.title: Schneider relève ses objectifs 2026 après un T3 record porté par les centres de données
item.description: Schneider Electric a relevé vendredi pour la deuxième fois de l’année ses objectifs de résultat d'exploitation et de chiffre d’affaires 2026, porté par la demande des géants du cloud pour les centres de données dédiés à l’intelligence artificielle.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Huchet, Mathias Rozario
item.content:encoded: Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) a relevé vendredi pour la deuxième fois de l’année ses objectifs de résultat d'exploitation et de chiffre d’affaires 2026, porté par la demande des géants du cloud pour les centres de données dédiés à l’intelligence artificielle. Le fabricant français d'équipements électriques vise désormais une croissance organique de son Ebita comprise entre 18% et 21%, contre 14% à 19% auparavant, et de son chiffre d’affaires de 12% à 14%, contre 10% à 13% précédemment. Au troisième trimestre, le chiffre d’affaires de Schneider Electric a atteint 11,46 milliards d’euros, en hausse organique de 16,9%, dépassant les attentes des analystes qui tablaient sur 11,13 milliards d’euros, selon un consensus fourni par le groupe. S'exprimant lors d'une conférence de presse, le directeur financier Nathan Fast a qualifié le troisième trimestre de "meilleur (...) de l'histoire" du groupe. À Paris, vers 7h22 GMT, l'action était cependant en baisse de 1,43%. Les analystes de JPMorgan jugent les résultats solides, mais soulignent dans une note qu’un dépassement des attentes et un relèvement des objectifs étaient largement anticipés, le point médian des nouvelles prévisions étant globalement conforme au consensus. Le courtier estime également que l’incertitude entourant une éventuelle augmentation de capital pour financer l’acquisition de PTC pèse sur le titre. Selon Joachimm Klement, analyste chez Panmure Liberum, "ces résultats sont très solides, manifestement portés par la forte demande liée aux centres de données, qui devrait selon nous s’essouffler en 2027 et 2028". Si les investissements des géants américains du "cloud" continuent de soutenir l’activité, la région Chine et Asie de l’Est a enregistré la plus forte croissance organique des ventes au trimestre, à 26,1%, devant l’Amérique du Nord, à 19,9%. PRUDENCE SUR LE MOYEN-ORIENT En Chine, les centres de données ont porté la croissance, grâce aux ventes directes aux grands acteurs des réseaux sociaux, des technologies et des infrastructures numériques, ainsi qu’aux opérateurs nationaux et régionaux proposant de l’hébergement informatique mutualisé. Le groupe reste toutefois prudent concernant le Moyen-Orient, les tensions étant "susceptibles d'impacter le quatrième trimestre, avec un risque de pression potentielle sur les chaînes d’approvisionnement mondiales et d’augmentation de l’inflation" précise le communiqué. L’activité Gestion de l’énergie a vu ses ventes progresser de 18,8% en données organiques, tandis que celles des Automatismes industriels ont augmenté de 8,1%. Lors d'un échange avec la presse, le directeur financier du groupe Nathan Fast a confirmé que la marque PTC (PTC.O) devrait être conservée après [USN:FWN45R02X TEXT:"l’acquisition"], avec une gouvernance et une structure similaires à Aveva.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Hausse en vue en Europe, sauf à Londres, après les turbulences dans la "tech" (actualisé)
item.description: Les principales Bourses européennes, à l'exception de la place londonienne, devraient poursuivre leur rebond vendredi à l'ouverture après les turbulences dans le secteur de l'intelligence artificielle (IA) à la suite de la débâcle de CoreWeave .
item.dc:creator: Claude Chendjou
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes, à l'exception de la place londonienne, devraient poursuivre leur rebond vendredi à l'ouverture après les turbulences dans le secteur de l'intelligence artificielle (IA) à la suite de la débâcle de CoreWeave (CRWV.O) . D'après les premières indications disponibles, le CAC 40 parisien (.FCHI) devrait gagner 0,35% à l'ouverture. Le Dax (.GDAXI) à Francfort pourrait avancer de 0,48%, tandis que le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) à Londres devrait refluer de 0,27%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) est attendu en progression de 0,49% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) en hausse de 0,23%. Les marchés actions devraient progresser avec la stabilisation dans l'obligataire à la suite de la chute des rendements jeudi, les traders s'étant rués sur les bons du Trésor américain et d'autres titres souverains considérés comme des actifs refuges. Le dollar s'achemine vers sa première perte hebdomadaire en cinq semaines, la baisse des rendements américains ayant érodé l'attrait pour le billet vert. Parallèlement, l'or recule par rapport à son pic de jeudi, tandis que le pétrole Brent reflue vers les 105 dollars le baril, signe d'un regain d'appétit pour le risque. L'opérateur de centres de données CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , déficitaire, doit près de 50 milliards de dollars selon les données de LSEG, ce qui a déclenché jeudi une forte vague de ventes sur les valeurs technologiques aux Etats-Unis, en Asie et en Europe, semant la panique sur les marchés boursiers dans le monde. L'action CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , soutenue par Nvidia, a cependant retrouvé un peu de sérénité jeudi soir. "Les marchés mondiaux redeviennent très agités après une période de faible volatilité: Wall Street est en proie à des fluctuations brutales, les rendements obligataires oscillent, les marchés des devises font des pirouettes et les cours des matières premières partent dans toutes les directions", écrit dans une note Kyle Rodda, analyste marchés chez Capital.com. "Les marchés mondiaux pourraient bien connaître une période prolongée de ce type de volatilité" alors que les annonces de résultats des entreprises technologiques sont attendues dans les semaines à venir et que les marchés tentent également d'anticiper la trajectoire des taux directeurs aux États-Unis et dans d'autres grandes économies, a-t-il ajouté. Le président de la Réserve fédérale, Kevin Warsh, s'est montré très discret vendredi sur l'évolution de la politique monétaire. D'autres responsables des grandes banques centrales doivent s'exprimer lors d'événements organisés dans le cadre des assemblées annuelles du FMI et de la Banque mondiale à Bangkok au cours de la journée. Les investisseurs doivent analyser ce vendredi une salve de résultats d'entreprises, dont ceux de [USN:S8N41X06M TEXT:"Schneider Electric"] (SCHN.PA) , d'ABB et General Motors, après la publication en début de semaine des comptes des groupes financiers américains. Côté indicateurs économiques, les deux rendez-vous du jour sont les chiffres de l'inflation définitive de la zone euro pour le mois de septembre et les données de la production industrielle américaine du mois dernier. A WALL STREET La Bourse de New York a fini en hausse jeudi, rebondissant après deux séances dans le rouge et des pertes initiales, alors que les gains du secteur des soins de santé ont relégué au second plan la préoccupation des investisseurs à propos de l'IA et des entreprises concernées. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a gagné 1,08% à 52.177,69 points. Le S&P-500 (.SPX) , plus large, a pris 0,33% à 7.744,06 points. Le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a avancé de son côté de 0,08% à 26.713,03 points. EN ASIE A la Bourse de Tokyo, l'indice Nikkei (.N225) a rebondi vendredi de 1,39% à 65.324,29 points, tandis que le Topix (.TOPX) , plus large, a pris 1,67% à 4.066,00 points. Le marché japonais s'est redressé après six séances consécutives de baisse, mais les gains ont été limités par la prudence des investisseurs à l'approche de la publication des résultats des entreprises et des élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis. L'indice de référence taïwanais (.TWII) progresse de 0,30% et l'indice Hang Seng de Hong Kong (.HSI) monte de 0,40%, les gains étant désormais réduits par rapport à l'ouverture des marchés. En Chine, le SSE Composite (.SSEC) de Shanghai reflue de 0,33% et le CSI 300 (.CSI300) fléchit de 0,53% dans une séance volatile où les indices ont un temps rebondi après être tombés la veille à un creux de 14 mois. La tendance positive a un temps été soutenue par les entreprises d'IA qui ont dévoilé des plans de rachats d'actions et des prévisions de croissance exceptionnelle, mais elle a fini par s'essouffler. LES VALEURS A SUIVRE EN EUROPE: [USN:L8N46123L] CHANGES/TAUX Le dollar recule de 0,16% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , se dirigeant vers sa première baisse hebdomadaire en cinq semaines. L'euro grignote 0,12%, à 1,1232 dollar, tandis que la livre sterling s'échange à 1,3307 dollar (+0,26%). Le rendement des bons du Trésor américain à dix ans est à l'équilibre, s'affichant à 5,08%. Sur l'ensemble de la semaine, il devrait enregistrer sa plus forte baisse hebdomadaire depuis plus d'un an en raison d'une ruée vers les obligations considérées comme des actifs refuge. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans fait également du surplace, à 3,41%, après une baisse de près de six points de base la veille. PÉTROLE Le marché pétrolier est en repli vendredi mais devrait enregistrer des gains hebdomadaires en raison de l'incertitude concernant les approvisionnements en provenance du Moyen-Orient et d'une baisse plus importante que prévu des stocks de brut aux Etats-Unis la semaine dernière. Le Brent reflue de 0,42% à 105,47 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) décline de 0,43% à 97,55 dollars . Sur l'ensemble de la semaine, le Brent devrait gagner 0,44% et le WTI 5,81%. item.title: Russia takes control of more European corporate assets ahead of Zelenskiy's appearance at EU summit
item.description: Russia has moved to place local assets of French, German, Swedish, and Belgian companies under temporary management, according to a decree by President Vladimir Putin, as EU ties hit a new low over the bloc's support for Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia has moved to place local assets of French, German, Swedish, and Belgian companies under temporary management, according to a decree by President Vladimir Putin, as EU ties hit a new low over the bloc's support for Ukraine. Thursday's decree listed assets belonging to French flooring maker Tarkett, German packaging maker Menshen, Swedish packaging maker Sverige International Holdings and Belgian hygiene product company Ontex (ONTEX.BR) . It also listed Russian assets of former European metal-packaging business Eviosys acquired by US packaging group Sonoco (SON.N) in December 2024. The decree listed the assets as owned by Sonoco's Dutch unit. The Kremlin said earlier that such measures to take control over foreign firms were a response to EU nations' involvement in "direct battlefield hostilities" but stressed they were "reversible." The latest move against European companies came ahead of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's appearance at an EU summit on Friday and amid reports that the United States could seek control of some Russian assets frozen in Europe. Russia criticises the EU for [USN:L6N3XO0R3 TEXT:"freezing"] about €210 billion ($238 billion) of its sovereign assets in response to the war and for targeting assets belonging to Russian companies in Europe and other Western countries. The new decree follows a similar [USN:L1N45L0FF TEXT:"move"] last month against food giant Nestle (NESN.S) and retailers Auchan and Metro (B4B0n.H) .

item.title: Security stepped up in India's capital for 'cockroach' movement rally
item.description: Police warned of traffic disruptions in the Indian capital because of the latest in a series of protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Security was stepped up and police warned of traffic disruptions in the Indian capital Delhi on Friday as the 'cockroach' movement called for a rally in the central business district, its latest in a series of protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief. The youth-led 'Cockroach Janta Party', opposition groups, and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner [USN:P8N44T0DC TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation over a [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists"] that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called Friday's flag protest in support of [USN:L6N46006T TEXT:"two CJP leaders"] detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban. CJP and left-wing students groups have urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag. Delhi Police, however, urged people not to join "such assemblies", and the civic authority announced late on Thursday that the park itself would be closed for two days "due to administrative reasons". Police said they can facilitate a group of select people to carry the national flag and sing the national anthem at a "suitable place". Traders in the area petitioned the Supreme Court to prevent the protest, which they say "would cause severe loss", and demanded compensation for losses suffered during a similar rally planned over the weekend that was foiled by a security crackdown. The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the [USN:L6N46206J TEXT:"biggest political challenge"]s faced by Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power. A [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"weeks-long sit-in"] by its supporters earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam paper leaks. The latest demonstrations erupted after The Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems.

item.title: Schneider Electric raises 2026 targets again on booming data centre demand
item.description: Schneider Electric raised its 2026 core profit and revenue targets for the second time this year on Friday, as the French industrial group cements its role as a key supplier to big cloud companies building AI data centres.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Rozario, Matthieu Huchet
item.content:encoded: Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) raised its 2026 core profit and revenue targets for the second time this year on Friday, as the French industrial group cements its role as a key supplier to big cloud companies building AI data centres. Schneider expects its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization to grow between 18% and 21% organically in 2026, instead of the previously forecast 14% to 19%. It sees organic revenue growth between 12% and 14%, versus the earlier range of 10% to 13%. "Data Centers remained a key growth driver as we continue to execute on our backlog while seeing triple-digit demand growth in the quarter," CEO Olivier Blum said in a quarterly statement. Once mainly known for its circuit breakers and industrial electrical equipment, Schneider has emerged as one of the biggest industrial beneficiaries of the AI boom, building the backbone of data centres, supplying everything from cooling units and server racks to critical power distribution equipment. Third-quarter revenue grew 16.9% organically to €11.46 billion ($12.87 billion), beating analysts' average forecast of €11.13 billion in a company-provided consensus. "We delivered the strongest quarter in Schneider's history," finance chief Nathan Fast said during a press call. Orders for data centres are sustained by continued strong demand from US hyperscalers, though third-quarter growth was led by China and East Asia, Schneider said. The data centre business was the main growth driver in the region, both from direct sales to large customers in social media, technology and digital infrastructure, and from domestic and regional co-location customers, it added. Schneider is also building up its software offering with the recent acquisition of [USN:L6N432112 TEXT:"industrial AI specialist"] Cognite and the $22.6 billion deal [USN:L6N45Q07P TEXT:"to buy engineering software maker"] PTC (PTC.O) , as it seeks to create a platform spanning product design, industrial operations and energy management. The PTC brand will likely be operated under a similar governance structure as Schneider's industrial software unit Aveva, fully acquired in 2023, Fast said. Schneider shares were little moved in early trading. They have gained around 10% since the start of 2026, though the performance was dampened by a negative reaction to the PTC deal in early October. item.title: Hedge funds' role comes into focus following European bonds turmoil
item.description: A sharp sell-off in European government bonds this month shows how hedge funds' growing role is making a systemically important market more vulnerable — a risk regulators are watching closely.
